fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Paul says envy, strife, abusive talk and evil suspicions come out of those controversies and disputes about words. That's a whole basket of trouble. Nobody walks away from a word fight with a trophy.

That sounds lovely, friend, but it's not what Paul says. He says these men regard godliness as a means of gain. Notice who he's talking about: men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. Peace isn't the word he uses for what they see in it.

Paul actually says it, friend. He says those many foolish and harmful desires "…plunge them into ruin and destruction." It's in the verse about those who want to be rich. So the statement is true. It's a heavy line.
You've got it, friend. Paul says that by craving money, some have "…pierced themselves with many sorrows." Themselves! That's a hard line to read. Better to catch it early.
Paul doesn't blame friends, friend. He says that by craving money, some "…pierced themselves with many sorrows." Nobody else is in the verse holding the point. I think this one hurts.
